Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Task 37f0b9db: orthogonal bridges between repeated markers

## Rule supported by demo and solved test
In a mostly uniform grid, identify the repeated marker color (demo: 6; test: 2) and the bridge/fill color (demo: 3). For each row, between the leftmost and rightmost marker of that color, recolor intervening background cells to the fill color. Do the same in each column between its topmost and bottommost marker. Retain all original marker cells and all cells outside these spans. The bridge is bounded by the extreme markers: do not extend beyond them. Crossings are simply the union of horizontal and vertical spans.

## Evidence and validation
Demo 10x4: color 6 markers define bridge spans. Example row 4 (0-indexed) has 6 at columns 0 and 3, with columns 1–2 changed to 3. Column 0 markers at rows 2,4,7 bound fill at rows 3,5,6. Sparse unrelated markers/background remain unchanged outside bounded spans.
Solved test 7x24: background 5, marker 2, fill 3. Apply spans over background cells only, preserving marker cells. The resulting grid was accepted.

## Procedure
1. Infer marker, background, and fill colors from the current pair(s); colors may differ across instances.
2. For every row and column containing at least two marker cells, fill only background cells strictly between the extreme marker coordinates.
3. Do not use adjacent-marker-only pairing, draw outward rays, fill all grid lines, or overwrite marker cells.
4. Validate dimensions and mechanically compare the changed-cell set against the bounded row/column span union.
